name: AOGLine
summary: A fictional recovery desk for aircraft on the ground. It is sample data, not a product you can buy.
paragraphs: AOGLine, in this sample, ranks parts, loaner engines, and ferry options when an aircraft is down. It is built here so the directory has a page shape. There is no company by this name behind the listing.
A real listing in this slot would say what the tool actually does, who it is for, and what it costs. This page shows the fields. It does not describe a live service.
whyItMatters: An airline or MRO would only keep a tool like this if a planner's check of past AOG events got shorter, and the saved aircraft time covered the subscription more than once.
pricing: Sample pricing, not a live offer.
bestFor: A maintenance control desk that wants to see the directory format, not a vendor to call.
